turns.prompt_text: I'm running the MacBook Air and I have a window that will not close. How do I close it?
turns.response_html:
It can be incredibly frustrating when a window or an entire application hangs and refuses to close. Since the standard red "X" button or Command + W isn't working, you likely need to "Force Quit" the application.

Here are the most effective ways to handle a frozen window on your MacBook Air:

1. The Keyboard Shortcut (Fastest)

The quickest way to bring up the management menu is to use this key combination: Command ($\mathscr{H}$) + Option ($\tau$) + Escape (Esc)

  • A small window will appear listing all open applications.
  • Select the app that is giving you trouble.
  • Click Force Quit.
  • Confirm the action in the pop-up.

2. The Apple Menu

If you prefer using the mouse:

  1. Click the Apple Logo ($\apple$) in the top-left corner of your screen.
  2. Select Force Quit... from the dropdown menu.
  3. Choose the stubborn application and click Force Quit.

3. The Dock Method

If you know exactly which app the window belongs to:

  1. Find the app's icon in your Dock at the bottom of the screen.
  2. Right-click (or Control-click) the icon.
  3. Hold down the Option ($\tau$) key on your keyboard.
  4. The "Quit" option will change to Force Quit. Click it.

4. Activity Monitor (The "Nuclear" Option)

If the window belongs to a background process or the app doesn't show up in the Force Quit list:

  1. Press Command + Space to open Spotlight and type "Activity Monitor", then hit Enter.
  2. Find the process name in the list.
  3. Click the "X" icon at the very top of the Activity Monitor window.
  4. Select Force Quit.

If the entire screen is frozen:

If you can't move your mouse or use the menus at all, hold down the Touch ID / Power button on the top-right of your keyboard for about 10 seconds until the screen goes black. Then, press it again to restart.
